findings.title: Pause and Delete disappear from the alert list menu
findings.body: In the list view `rulerRule` is now always undefined, but the Pause item is gated on `rulerRuleType.grafana.rule(rulerRule)` here and the Delete item is gated on `rulerRule` at line 165. The new Grafana (promRule) abilities compute canPause/canDelete as allowed, yet the menu items are never rendered, so users lose pause and delete from the list view (they only remain on the details page). The regression is locked in by GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx line 207, which asserts exactly 4 menu items, and the `ui.menuItems.delete` helper defined in that test is never used. The menu gating needs to use the promRule path for these actions, or the abilities should not be advertised.

findings.title: Delete item is gated on rulerRule, which is always absent in the list view
findings.body: `{canDelete && rulerRule && (...)}` hides Delete whenever rulerRule is undefined. Since the list view no longer fetches ruler rules, Delete is never shown for Grafana rules there even when the user has delete permission on the folder and canDelete is true via the promRule abilities. Delete is silently removed from the list view.

findings.title: Silence menu item in the list view does nothing
findings.body: In the list view `rule` (the RulerRuleDTO) is undefined. AlertRuleMenu shows the Silence item based on the Grafana promRule silence ability, and clicking it calls handleSilence, which sets showSilenceDrawer to true. But the drawer is rendered only when `rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule)` is true, which is false when rule is undefined. Also SilenceGrafanaRuleDrawer is passed `rulerRule`, which doesn't exist here. The result is a visible, permitted Silence action that silently does nothing. The drawer needs to be driven from promRule, or the menu item must be hidden when no ruler rule is present.

findings.title: GrafanaRuleListItem in the filter list has no key
findings.body: The diff removed `key={key}` from the grafana branch of the rules.map in FilterView, while the datasource and default branches still set key. React will warn about missing keys for this list and can misreconcile rows when the list grows or items reorder, because row identity and component state are no longer tied to the stable key computed by getRuleKey.

findings.title: Federated rule group check dropped from useAllAlertRuleAbilities
findings.body: useAllAlertRuleAbilities previously computed `isFederated = isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group)`. It now delegates to useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which only has the group identifier and hardcodes `const isFederated = false` here. Every caller of useAlertRuleAbility, useAlertRuleAbilities and useAllAlertRuleAbilities therefore loses the immutability check for federated groups, so Update, Delete, Pause and related actions can be enabled for federated rules that cannot be modified.

findings.title: Duplicate becomes allowed for non-Grafana rules via skipToken
findings.body: When promRule is not a Grafana rule, AlertRuleMenu and RuleActionsButtons pass skipToken, so useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities receives undefined. With no rule, MaybeSupported is AlwaysSupported and isPluginProvided is false, so Duplicate returns [true, user has AlertingRuleCreate]. AlertRuleMenu ORs this with the ruler-based ability (canDuplicate = ruler || grafana), so any data source rule in the list shows Duplicate for users with Grafana create permission. This bypasses the ruler-availability check and the plugin-provided check (the ruler path marks plugin-provided rules as unsupported). The grafana hook should return NotSupported when no rule is supplied.

findings.title: Grafana rule links drop returnTo, breaking navigation back to the filtered list
findings.body: The previous GrafanaRuleLoader built the view href with `{ returnTo }` from createReturnTo(). The new href is just createRelativeUrl(`/alerting/grafana/${uid}/view`), so navigating to a Grafana rule and back no longer returns to the filtered list. Data source rule links still pass returnTo, so behavior is now inconsistent between rule types. This is an unmentioned navigation regression.

findings.title: New Grafana promRule abilities hook has no direct test coverage
findings.body: useAllGrafanaPromRuleAbilities, useGrafanaPromRuleAbility(ies) and the skipToken path contain new permission logic that determines what the user can do in the list view (silence, export, duplicate, pause, delete). RulesTable.test.tsx mocks the whole hook surface, and GrafanaGroupLoader.test.tsx only checks that a few menu entries exist. None of the tests exercise the real decisions, including the skipToken/non-Grafana case where Duplicate is incorrectly allowed, or the federated check that was dropped.

findings.title: Comment says this is a copy of RuleActionsButtons.tsx, which is no longer true
findings.body: The header comment describes this file as a copy of RuleActionsButtons.tsx with only the View button removed. After this change it takes promRule, uses useGrafanaPromRuleAbility and getEditableIdentifier, and has different identifier and provenance logic, so it has diverged. The stale comment will mislead maintainers about which file to change.
